sensitive.label: high
sensitive.title:
Date of birth — high severity, confirmed
Reported because it passed plausible_dob.
Special-risk identifier in combination with a name. Only dates near an explicit birth-date label are reported, so an unlabelled DOB is missed.

sensitive.label: high
sensitive.title:
National Insurance number — high severity, confirmed
Reported because it passed ni_prefix.
A direct identifier under UK data protection law. Uniquely identifies an individual and is routinely treated as high risk in a breach assessment.

sensitive.label: medium
sensitive.title:
Email address — medium severity, pattern
Reported on the pattern alone, with nothing else to confirm it.
Personal data whenever it identifies an individual, including firstname.lastname@ addresses at a corporate domain.

sensitive.label: medium
sensitive.title:
Phone number — medium severity, confirmed
Reported because it passed uk_phone.
Personal data when tied to an individual. UK formats; numbers with another country code are reported as international phone numbers.

sensitive.label: medium
sensitive.title:
Street address — medium severity, pattern
Reported on the pattern alone, with nothing else to confirm it.
Detected by house-number-and-street-word heuristics for English, Portuguese, Spanish, Italian, French, German and Dutch. It will miss flats, named houses and addresses split across lines.

sensitive.label: medium
sensitive.title:
UK postcode — medium severity, confirmed
Reported because it passed uk_postcode.
A full postcode narrows location to a handful of properties and is treated as personal data when combined with any other identifier.

sensitive.label: high
sensitive.title:
UK sort code — high severity, confirmed
Reported because it passed sort_code.
Financial identifier. On its own it identifies a bank branch; combined with an account number it enables direct debit fraud.

sensitive.label: high
sensitive.title:
UK bank account number — high severity, corroborated
Reported because it sits near "account number".
Financial identifier. Eight bare digits are far too common to report without a nearby label, so an unlabelled account number will not be found.

sensitive.label: high
sensitive.title:
IBAN — high severity, confirmed
Reported because it passed iban_mod97.
Financial identifier, validated here with the ISO 13616 mod-97 checksum, so false positives are rare.

sensitive.label: high
sensitive.title:
Payment card number — high severity, confirmed
Reported because it passed luhn, card_issuer.
Payment card data. Validated with the Luhn checksum and the issuing network's prefix and length. Storing this in unencrypted documents is a PCI DSS problem as well as a data protection one.

sensitive.label: low
sensitive.title:
UK VAT number — low severity, confirmed
Reported because it passed vat_mod97.
Business identifier. Personal data when the business is a sole trader.

sensitive.label: high
sensitive.title:
Unique Taxpayer Reference — high severity, corroborated
Reported because it sits near "utr".
HMRC taxpayer identifier. Ten bare digits are too common to report without a nearby label.

score.label: ready
score.method: weighted_sum: each signal's rating scores good=1.0, fair=0.5, poor=0.0; weights renormalised across the 14 signals that produced a rating for this document, then expressed out of 100.

signals.name: PDF form fields
signals.why: Named form fields give labelled values, with no layout guesswork.

signals.name: Column layout
signals.why: Extractors follow file order, which can interleave columns.

signals.name: Date format consistency
signals.reason: only 2 dates were found, which is too few to say anything about consistency
signals.why: Mixed formats force a parser to guess, and the guess changes the date.

signals.name: Encryption or password protection
signals.why: A password protected file cannot be opened by a pipeline at all.

signals.name: Distinct fonts
signals.why: Rules that find a field by how it looks break across many fonts.

signals.name: Fonts embedded
signals.why: A font neither embedded nor standard is substituted, shifting the layout.

signals.name: Garbled character rate
signals.why: Replacement characters and lost spaces mean the text is not what is on the page.

signals.name: Hyphenated line breaks
signals.reason: only 72 words of text were available, too few for a rate per 1,000 words
signals.why: Words split at line ends are indexed and embedded as two fragments.

signals.name: Page area that is image
signals.why: Images of text cannot be read directly; they need OCR or a vision model.

signals.name: Languages detected
signals.why: A pipeline tuned for one language handles a second one poorly.

signals.name: OCR confidence
signals.reason: OCR did not run on this document, so there is no recognition confidence to report. It runs where a page has no text layer
signals.why: Recognised text is a guess, and a low-confidence guess is wrong in the details.

signals.name: Page rotation flag
signals.why: A page stored sideways reads in the wrong order unless the tool corrects it.

signals.name: Distinct page sizes
signals.why: Mixed page sizes break any rule that finds a value by its position.

signals.name: Repeated page lines
signals.reason: only 1 pages carried text; repeated lines need at least 3
signals.why: Headers and footers repeated on every page put the same text into many chunks.

signals.name: Scan resolution
signals.reason: no page is mostly a scanned image, so there is no scan resolution to measure. Resolution is only meaningful where the page really is a picture
signals.why: Below about 200 DPI, OCR starts confusing digits in amounts and accounts.

signals.name: Estimated scan skew
signals.reason: no page was rasterised for this document, which happens when every page has a usable text layer and so is not a scan
signals.why: OCR accuracy drops quickly with skew, and table rows stop lining up.

signals.name: Tables detected
signals.why: Every table is another structure to teach a pipeline about.

signals.name: Deepest table header
signals.reason: no tables were detected, so there is no header to measure
signals.why: A header stacked several rows deep spreads one column's meaning across cells.

signals.name: Merged table cells
signals.reason: no tables were detected, so there are no cells to merge
signals.why: A merged cell breaks the grid, so values land in the wrong row or column.

signals.name: Text layer coverage
signals.why: A page with almost no text layer is an image of its content.

signals.name: Text layer present
signals.why: With no text layer every character must be recognised from an image.

signals.name: Unmapped glyphs
signals.why: Glyph codes and private-use characters are text that was not mapped to letters.

limitations.statement: 1 passage in 1 document read as instructions to a model and are hidden from a person reading the document. A model given this text reads them.
Hidden-text checks cover the text layer of PDFs and the formatting of Word and Excel files. Text inside images, which a vision model reads, is not checked. Instruction patterns are mostly English.
18 models are priced from a maintained third-party table taken on 2026-09-09. Those prices have not been checked against the provider's own page.

1 document have no fixed pagination until they are rendered, so their page count, page dimensions and any per-page cost figure are not measurements. Vision-path costs are reported as not applicable for them.
110 model entr(y/ies) in pricing.yaml carry no price and are switched off, so no cost was computed for them. complydoc does not invent prices; fill them in and set last_verified to include them.

factors.name: Content
factors.why: Whether the text can be got off the page at all.

factors.name: Cost path
factors.why: Text already on the page is nearly free to send to a model. A scan has to be recognised first, and a page that yields nothing has to go as an image, which costs far more.

factors.name: Exposure
factors.why: What these documents carry that should not leave, weighted by severity and by how good the evidence for each finding is.

quick_wins.detail: These carry identifiers that passed a checksum. Anything sent to a hosted model takes them with it.
quick_wins.effect: the strongest findings in the folder, by evidence and severity
quick_wins.title: Deal with the confirmed high-severity identifiers

quick_wins.detail: These carry pages with no text layer and nothing recognised from them. As they stand every such page has to be sent to a model as an image, which is the expensive path. Running with --ocr, or with a second engine via --compare-ocr-engine, may get text off them.
quick_wins.effect: 1 document would move onto the text path
quick_wins.title: Read the pages nothing came off

quick_wins.detail: These contain text a reader does not see that reads as instructions to a model. Each passage is on the Security page. Remove it from the file, or drop the flagged passages from the extracted text before it is sent.
quick_wins.effect: a model no longer receives instructions a reviewer cannot see
quick_wins.title: Remove hidden instructions before these reach a model
